messages:
maya: Customer ticket #4891 — they report missing 'policy_violation' and some 'session_end' events in their SIEM export for 2025-05-12. They say Console shows the events but the S3 export under s3://redwood-exports/prod/2025-05-12/ contains fewer records. Example session_id: se-77f2.

support_lead: Thanks. Can you confirm whether missing from the UI, the daily export, or both? Any sample S3 object keys or gz files we can inspect?

maya: Missing from the daily S3 export only. UI (live index) shows 3 policy_violation entries for se-77f2 but export only has the earlier session_start and one policy_violation. I downloaded part-00012.gz and attached. Key: prod/2025-05-12/part-00012.gz

carlos: Quick thought: did we recently change the forwarder schema mapping? I remember a migration that flattened nested user object (user.id -> user_id) in v3.4. If the customer's SIEM saved query filters on user.id presence, some events could be filtered out on ingest into SIEM.

liam (sre_oncall): We rolled audit-forwarder v3.4 to prod on 2025-05-11. Change-log: "flatten user object, normalize event_type names, add lifecycle tagging". Also, lifecycle rule update moved some older parts to GLACIER INTELLIGENT_TIER on 2025-05-10 for prefixes older than 7 days if tagged incorrectly. Two separate potential causes.

security-bot: audit-forwarder v3.4 deployed by deploy-bot
- image: ghcr.io/redwood/audit-forwarder:3.4
- migration-runner: v1.2
- kms_key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-rotate

deploy-bot: migration job audit-migrate-flatten-users completed on 2025-05-11 03:12:40 UTC (shard failures: 4/128)

maya: Important: the attach shows one gzip member with decryption warning when we tried to open it in the support sandbox logs: "WARN KMS: envelope decryption fallback used" but the object did still decompress. I re-run locally and got entries with both \"user\":{\"id\":...} and \"user_id\":... in different records.

carlos: That suggests the migration ran partially (some shards updated, some not). SIEM-forwarder or their ingestion pipeline might be applying a filter that expects only nested user.id and ignores user_id. Also if lifecycle moved some parts to Glacier and we didn't restore them, exports could be missing chunks.

maya: Repro steps I ran: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-exports/prod/2025-05-12/part-00012.gz /tmp/
gunzip -c part-00012.gz | jq -c '. | {event_time, session_id, event_type, user, user_id}' | grep se-77f2 | tee /tmp/se-77f2-rows.txt
```
Found lines: one row had user.id present, two rows had user_id only. The SIEM saved query is: `where user.id != null and event_type=\"policy_violation\"` so the user_id-only rows get dropped.

liam (sre_oncall): Also ran a prefix scan across the date window and found 6 parts for 2025-05-12 were already restored to GLACIER). Those objects currently need restoration (restore-in-progress for 48h) before we can re-run forwarder/backfill.

support_lead: So multiple causes: (A) partial schema migration -> events with user_id only; (B) lifecycle mis-tag -> some parts moved to Glacier and not present in immediate export. We need fast mitigation and a remediation plan.

carlos: Suggested mitigations:
- immediate: tell SIEM customers to broaden saved queries to check both fields: `where (user.id != null OR user_id != null) AND event_type=\"policy_violation\"` (one-liner to share)
- hotfix: forwarder v3.4.1 to add compatibility layer that emits both user.id and user_id during export, and ensure migration-runner retries failed shards
- remediation: backfill job that replays raw ingestion for 2025-05-10..2025-05-13 and writes normalized payloads to a remediation bucket; restore Glacier objects for affected prefixes first

maya: I kicked off an S3 inventory and scanned for any part-* files with tag lifecycle=misapplied. Found 6 keys in 2025-05-12 range flagged for restoration. I initiated expedited restores for the 6 objects (request IDs attached to the ticket).

liam (sre_oncall): I'll open INC-2025-198 and assign to eng-infra and eng-ml to triage migration-runner failures and add retries. Hotfix release plan: v3.4.1 with compatibility mapping + additional integration test for both nested and flat user schemas. Target: patch and canary in 4 hours.

support_lead: Support action: send targeted notice to affected customers with workaround query and ETA: "We identified a schema migration that partially applied and a mistaken lifecycle tag. We're restoring affected export parts and releasing a forwarder compatibility hotfix (v3.4.1). Estimated timeline: 24-48 hours for full remediation and backfill." Use ticket #4891.

carlos: Backfill approach details I propose:
```
# backfill pseudocode
for date in 2025-05-10..2025-05-13:
  for key in s3.list_keys(prefix=date):
    if key.storage_class in ['GLACIER', 'DEEP_ARCHIVE']:
      s3.restore_object(key)
      wait_until_restored(key)
    payloads = s3.get_object(key) # raw
    for p in payloads:
      normalized = normalize_user_field(p) # emit both nested and flat
      emit_to_remediation_bucket(normalized)
```
Also add a small check: ensure migration-runner marks shard status as success only after checksum/rowcounts match expected.

maya: I exported the 3 policy_violation rows we could find and attached remediation CSV to ticket #4891. Also included sample session_ids: se-77f2, se-88b9, se-12c3.

security-bot: created incident INC-2025-198 (audit-export-schema-lifecycle)

deploy-bot: hotfix branch created: gh/infra/audit-forwarder/hotfix/compat-user-fields -> CI queued

liam (sre_oncall): After hotfix we should run an integrity check: counts per session_id and per event_type for the 4-day window and compare Console vs Export vs Remediation bucket. Post results here.

support_lead: Agreed. Once restores complete and compatibility canary looks good, eng will run backfill and we'll validate. I'll draft the customer communication and update ticket. Marking P1 for support.

maya: Thanks all. I'll keep ticket updated and attach restore receipts. :thumbsup:
